operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.

values.description: values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

matchLabels.description: matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs.

schema.description: A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all resources.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of values, a key, and an operator.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.

values.description: values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

matchLabels.description: matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs.

policies.description: Ensures all Azure role assignments are made via Microsoft Entra PIM or explicitly approved apps; others are denied by default. Admins can allow exceptions for specific roles, users, or groups (e.g., break‑glass access). Existing role assignments are unaffected. Ensure your tenant has the required PIM licensing before enabling this policy; otherwise, access may be unintentionally blocked.
policies.display_name: Azure role assignment management should be restricted to Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management

metadata.description: Deny will block non-compliant role assignment requests. Audit will produce audit logs for non-compliant role assignment requests. When disabled no compliance evaluation will be done.

When it applies: If the user or service principle making the role assignment request (the requestor) has one of the object Ids listed here, the assignment management will be allowed outside PIM. Why to use: Include trusted users and service principles that manage role assignments as part of their normal operation. Note that these requesters will only be able to create active assignments outside of PIM. Values must be lowercase GUIDs.

When it applies: If the identity receiving the role assignment (the assignee) is of a principal type listed here, the assignment will not be blocked by the PIM-only policy. Why to use: Add types here that you do not require to go through PIM for role assignments. For example, include ServicePrincipal to allow assigning roles to application identities directly, or Group to permit group-based role assignments outside PIM.

When it applies: If the identity making the role assignment request (the requestor) is of a principal type listed here, the assignment management will be allowed outside PIM. Why to use: Permit certain principal types (e.g., ServicePrincipal for automation pipelines, or ForeignGroup for cross-tenant scenarios) to create role assignments directly, since those identities typically cannot interact with PIM.

When it applies: If a role definition ID appears in this list, the policy will not enforce PIM for assignment management to that role — the assignment is permitted even outside PIM. Why to use: Add roles here that are considered low-risk or operationally necessary to assign directly (e.g., Reader), so they can bypass the PIM requirement.Values must be lowercase GUIDs.

policies.description: Public IP Prefixes can be configured to be either Zone Aligned, Zone Redundant, or neither. metadata.description: This parameter lets you choose what type of Zone Resilience you want to allow. Aligned will identify any resources that are not configured as Zone Aligned as non-compliant resources. Redundant will identify any resources that are not configured to be Zone Redundant as non-compliant resources. Both (default), will identify any resource configurations that are not Zone Aligned or Zone Redundant as non-compliant resources.

This parameter lets you choose the effect of the policy. If you choose Audit (default), the policy will only audit resources for compliance. If you choose Deny, the policy will deny the creation of non-compliant resources. If you choose Disabled, the policy will not enforce compliance (useful, for example, as a second assignment to ignore a subset of non-compliant resources in a single resource group).

Label query to select Kubernetes resources for policy evaluation. An empty label selector matches all Kubernetes resources.

schema.description: A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all resources.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of values, a key, and an operator.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.

values.description: values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

matchLabels.description: matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs.

policies.description: Public IP addresses can be configured to be either Zone Aligned, Zone Redundant, or neither. This policy helps identify and enforce these resilience configurations.

metadata.description: This parameter lets you choose what type of Zone Resilience you want to allow. Aligned will identify any resources that are not configured as Zone Aligned as non-compliant resources. Redundant will identify any resources that are not configured to be Zone Redundant as non-compliant resources. Both (default), will identify any resource configurations that are not Zone Aligned or Zone Redundant as non-compliant resources.

This parameter lets you choose the effect of the policy. If you choose Audit (default), the policy will only audit resources for compliance. If you choose Deny, the policy will deny the creation of non-compliant resources. If you choose Disabled, the policy will not enforce compliance (useful, for example, as a second assignment to ignore a subset of non-compliant resources in a single resource group).

List of Kubernetes namespaces to exclude from policy evaluation. System namespaces "kube-system", "gatekeeper-system" and "azure-arc" are always excluded by design. "azure-extensions-usage-system" is optional to remove.

Label query to select Kubernetes resources for policy evaluation. An empty label selector matches all Kubernetes resources.

schema.description: A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all resources.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of values, a key, and an operator.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.

values.description: Values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array should not be empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

matchLabels.description: matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs.

metadata.description: List of Kubernetes namespaces to only include in policy evaluation. An empty list means the policy is applied to all resources in all namespaces.

The source k8s object for constraint evaluation. 'Original' means only evaluate against the specific GroupVersionKind specified in the policy definition. It is recommended that users use the fully-qualified Docker image name (e.g. start with a domain name) in order to avoid unexpectedly exempting images from an untrusted repository.

Label query to select Kubernetes resources for policy evaluation. An empty label selector matches all Kubernetes resources.

schema.description: A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all resources.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of values, a key, and an operator.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.

values.description: values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

matchLabels.description: matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs.

metadata.description: List of Kubernetes namespaces to only include in policy evaluation. An empty list means the policy is applied to all resources in all namespaces.

Label query to select Kubernetes resources for policy evaluation. An empty label selector matches all Kubernetes resources.

schema.description: A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all resources.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of values, a key, and an operator.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.

values.description: values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

matchLabels.description: matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs.
